items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: Horace left his band this summer of 1928 and went out to Chicago to play piano in Sammy Stewart's orchestra

ctx.x: I would like, since we have a little more time, and a little more tape here, in going over, especially some of the material from the book and Hendersononia. There are some quotes in here that were basically in the area where, the pages that were dealing more with you, and, first of all, there -- you might be able to clear up some things concerning questions of personnel in various bands at various times, and I'll just read a graph to you here.

It says, "There are other reports that Horace left his band this summer of 1928 and went out to Chicago to play piano in Sammy Stewart's orchestra," which we talked about on our first tape, "Including some dates in Columbus, Ohio. but that fall Horace left Stewart and decided to form a new

band of his own. He sent to Indianapolis for Raymond Syd Valentine (trumpet, and leader of the Patent Leather Kids of Gennett record fame) and Cleve Bottoms on alto sax. Duncan Schiedt dates this as late 1928, when the band was in Columbus, Ohio. The new personnel was given as: Syd Valentine, Red Harland, Sprat Morton, playing trumpets." And then here it says, "Unknown trombones." Do you know who the trombones were at that time? You're in Columbus, Ohio, 1928, Syd Valentine.
